stem.text: Does the series \( \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{6}{\left(n + 2\right) \left(n + 3\right)} \) converge? If it does, find its sum.

answer_key.label: The series converges, and its sum is \( 2 \).

worked_solution.text: Each term splits as \( \frac{6}{\left(n + 2\right) \left(n + 3\right)} = \frac{6}{n + 2} - \frac{6}{n + 3} \), so in the nth partial sum every middle term cancels and \( S_n = 2 - \frac{6}{n + 3} \).
worked_solution.rule_named: partial sums of a telescoping series

worked_solution.text: A series converges exactly when its partial sums approach a finite limit. Here \( \lim_{n \to \infty} S_n = 2 \), so the series converges and its sum is \( 2 \).
worked_solution.rule_named: convergence as the limit of the partial sums
